---
title: "Research Presentation Template (Quarto)"
description: "The group's branded Quarto slide template, and how to install Quarto to use it."
categories: [Software, Quarto, Presentations]
---

A [Quarto](https://quarto.org) revealjs template for talks, defenses and group meetings: Western
purple headings, a footer with the Western Engineering logo, and a fixed 16:9 slide size that
doesn't reflow or "float" the way a plain web page does. Titles sit in a consistent header
position at the top of every slide, following the
[Assertion-Evidence](https://www.assertion-evidence.com/) approach to research-slide design.

## Download

[**Download the template (.zip)**](presentation-template-files/presentation-template.zip)

Unzip it wherever you keep the talk, and rename `template.qmd` to something meaningful (e.g.
`slides.qmd`). It's four files: the slide source (`template.qmd`), the theme
(`theme.scss`), the Western Engineering logo (`img/logo.png`), and a `README.md` with
maintainer-level notes on the CSS if you need to customize the layout further.

To browse the source instead, or grab a single file, it's in the repository at
[`templates/presentation/`](https://github.com/DeGrootResearchGroup/GroupResources/tree/main/templates/presentation).

## Install Quarto

Quarto is a free command-line tool; you don't need R or Python to build slides with it.

1. Download the installer for your OS from
   [quarto.org/docs/get-started](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) and run it.
2. Open a terminal (**Terminal** on macOS, **PowerShell** on Windows) and confirm it installed:

   ```bash
   quarto check
   ```

   This prints Quarto's version and confirms it can find a browser to preview in — that's all you
   need for this template (its checks for TeX/Jupyter/knitr don't matter here since the template
   has no executable code).
3. Optional but recommended: install the
   [Quarto extension for VS Code](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=quarto.quarto)
   if you edit in VS Code — it adds a live preview pane and syntax highlighting for `.qmd` files.

## Render and preview

From a terminal, `cd` into the folder you unzipped, then:

```bash
quarto preview slides.qmd
```

This opens the deck in your browser and reloads it automatically as you edit and save. Use the
arrow keys or space bar to move between slides, `s` to open speaker notes, and `f` for fullscreen.

## Customize

Edit the YAML at the top of `slides.qmd`:

```yaml
title: "Your Talk Title"
author: "Your Name"
institute: "Your Department<br>Western University"
footer: "Your conference or committee name"
```

Then replace the example slides with your own content. Two-column layouts
(`::: {.columns}` / `::: {.column width="50%"}`), math (`$...$`), code blocks and speaker notes
(`::: {.notes}`) are all demonstrated in the template — copy whichever pattern you need.

To change colours, fonts or the footer layout, edit `theme.scss`; it's plain CSS with comments
explaining the less obvious parts. To use a different logo, replace `img/logo.png` and update the
`logo:` path in the YAML if you rename it.

## Export to PDF

For a PDF you can email or upload (a defense committee, a conference submission), use
[decktape](https://github.com/astefanutti/decktape), which drives a real reveal.js presentation
page-by-page rather than relying on browser print layout:

```bash
npx decktape reveal slides.html slides.pdf
```

This needs [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) installed (`npx` comes with it) — check with `node -v` in
your terminal, or install it from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org) if that command isn't found. You
can also print the deck manually from a browser — see `README.md` in the download for the
alternative and its trade-offs.
